body.name: finite mixed-statistic and common-marginal calculation
body.construction: Let \(\epsilon=1/4\), \(d=2\), \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \(e_1=e_2=1/2\), and \(\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0\). For \(n=m=1\), independence of the samples gives \[E\!\left[2\mathbf 1\{\mathcal L_1=((1,1,1))\}\left(\mathbf 1\{\mathcal U_1=((1,0))\}+\mathbf 1\{\mathcal U_1=((1,1))\}\right)\right]=2q_{11}p_1.\] At \(\mu_{11}=1\), this equals \(1/4\), while the treated cell target is \(p_1\mu_{11}=1/2\). Define \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\) to put unit mass on the law with \(\mu_{11}=\mu_{12}=0\), and define \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\) to put unit mass on the law with \(\mu_{11}=1\) and \(\mu_{12}=0\). Under both priors, \(P_{XA}(x,a)=1/4\) for all \((x,a)\), whereas \(\tau(P)=0\) under \(\Pi_0^{\mathrm{small}}\) and \(\tau(P)=1/2\) under \(\Pi_1^{\mathrm{small}}\); consequently the auxiliary laws agree for every \(m\), and the total variation distance between the two labeled laws is \(1-(3/4)^n\). These identities constitute \(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{small}}\).
